teams.synopsis: Back in a place not seen since 2023 - a 141-point Week 1 with underrated depth once Terry shakes off the rust.
teams.blurb: Back in a place we haven't seen since 2023, LP looks like they're in prime form with a 141-point Week 1. The Fields-Wilson stack is clicking, the RB duo is strong, and Laporta is back to his old self. The team has underrated depth, and once Terry shakes off the rust, it's go time. Projected record: 10-4.

teams.synopsis: Primed to repeat in '25 after the Week 1 blowout - stacking looks like the early-season strategy of choice.
teams.blurb: After the Week 1 blowout, Grits looks primed to repeat in '25. Assuming the Bowers injury is minor, the only real weakness is RB2. However, I believe by Week 7, RJ Harvey could regularly be projected in the low-mid teens. The Baker-Egbuka stack also looks lethal - which is good for Grits, because stacking looks like the strategy early on. Projected record: 10-4.

teams.synopsis: Etienne Jr. looks like a massive steal in Coen's offense - the WRs are the last key to pushing this team to the top.
teams.blurb: I don't want to jump the gun, but Etienne Jr. looks like a massive steal for MFGA in Coen's Jacksonville offense. RPM has a couple of TEs to rotate, Lamar looks great, and the RBs are trustworthy, leaving the WRs as the key to pushing this team to the top of the PFFL. Projected record: 10-4.

teams.synopsis: The biggest riser in projected wins - Hollywood should keep feasting while Worthy is sidelined.
teams.blurb: The biggest riser in projected wins, STD looks set for another win in Week 2 against a shaken-up BLR squad. Hollywood should keep feasting while Worthy is out, and A.J. should rebound. With a strong bench, this franchise looks ready for another successful season. Projected record: 9-5.

teams.synopsis: A glaring RB2 hole, but a Josh Allen-led Week 1 win got this team on track before a tough Harvey matchup.
teams.blurb: The team has a glaring problem at RB2, but the rest of the starting lineup looks solid and could be competitive this season. A big Week 1 win led by Josh Allen got them on track, but a tough Week 2 matchup against Harvey will test their abilities. Projected record: 8-6.

teams.synopsis: A fan of the WR trio that put up 61 combined in Week 1 - the revolving door at QB/TE is the swing factor.
teams.blurb: I'm a fan of the WR trio of <mark class="hl-player">Ladd</mark>, <mark class="hl-player">JSN</mark>, and <mark class="hl-player">Flowers</mark>, who combined for 61 points in Week 1. There's a revolving door at QB and TE, but if the team can find consistent production there, they could be competitive in 2025. That might be put on hold for now with a tough Week 2 matchup.

teams.synopsis: Right where expected, floating between 3rd and 7th - a top-10 TE addition could restart a contending season.
teams.blurb: Just where I expect The Minutemen to be, floating between 3rd and 7th for most of the season. A strong starting lineup and bench, aside from Loveland, make them a tough matchup each week. If they acquire a top-10 TE, another contending season isn't out of the question. Projected record: 8-6.

teams.synopsis: One of the few teams the writer's happy with from last week - the RB duo remains the one concern heading forward.
teams.blurb: One of the few teams I'm happy with from last week's rankings. They have an exciting Week 2 matchup, and I expect some positive regression from Harvey's WRs after a poor Week 1. My main concern for the season is the RB duo - a trade seems inevitable. Projected record: 7-7.

teams.synopsis: A rough fall from 1st after just 83 points - still pulled out the win, and a bounce back looks likely.
teams.blurb: Maybe just as rough a fall as BLR's. After starting at 1st, TTF put up only 83 points in Week 1 but still pulled out the win. Scoring -2 from D/ST and K isn't ideal, but it shows how easily this team can improve. With a 125-point projection, a bounce-back feels likely. Expect a rise next week. Projected record: 7-7.

teams.synopsis: A tight Week 1 loss, but Judkins activated and a resurgent Deebo could keep this team from missing a beat.
teams.blurb: I still don't get this team name, but after a tight Week 1 loss, GTG looks to bounce back against RWB. The Kittle injury hurts, but with Judkins activated and Deebo looking like his '21 self, this team might not miss a beat. A TE may need to be acquired if Otton can't produce. Projected record: 5-9.

teams.synopsis: Proved they're not the worst team in the league - the Burrow trade leaves TE as the only real hole left.
teams.blurb: It was only up from there as RWB proved they are not the worst team in the league. Hopefully the London injury is minor so this team can be fully healthy in Week 2 and get their first win. After the Burrow trade, the only position holding them back from being a top team is TE. Projected record: 5-9.

teams.synopsis: Dropped from 2nd to 12th, maybe too harshly - an Engram injury on top of the Rashee suspension makes it tougher.
teams.blurb: Maybe I am being too harsh dropping BLR from 2nd to 12th, but we'll see in Week 2. The WRs were nonexistent in Week 1, and an Engram injury on top of Rashee's six-week suspension makes surviving the first half of the season even tougher. Projected record: 5-9.

teams.synopsis: Hadn't lost to their rival since the 2020 playoffs, until now - a Burrow trade brings new WRs to test in Week 2.
teams.blurb: This team hasn't lost to their rival since the 2020 playoffs... until now. New York put up a dud in Week 1 with its three WRs combining for less than 15 points, and after a big trade sending Burrow to RWB, we'll see if the new WRs from the deal can help secure a win in Week 2. Projected record: 4-10.

teams.synopsis: Not high on this team to begin with, and Week 1 didn't change that - could this be Pitts Sr.'s year regardless?
teams.blurb: I was not high on this team coming into the season, and Week 1 did nothing to change my mind. The Worthy injury is something to monitor, but if Warren can step in and produce, maybe this team can stay competitive without making trades. Could this finally be Pitts Sr.'s year? Projected record: 2-12.
